title: Optimized Macherey-Nagel NucleoSpin Tissue Protocol for Environmental DNA Extraction
author: Michaela Harris
materials: If not using disposable equipment, rinse tweezers, scissors, and weigh boats with water, 0.5% sodium hypochlorite solution, and water for final rinse during at least 00:00:30 , and ethanol (i.e., to dry equipment and avoid rust). Change gloves. Repeat steps 3 to 6 for each filter.

steps.title: Prepare Workspace and Materials
steps.instruction: Clean the benchtop and organize all necessary materials.

substeps.instruction: Clean bench with water, 0.5% sodium hypochlorite solution, and water; OR clean with water, Alconox, 0.5% sodium hypochlorite solution, and ethanol.
Install 2 mL microtubes with Lyse&Spin baskets, pre-identified 2 mL Eppendorf Safe-Lock tubes, tweezers, scissors, weigh boats, waste beaker, microtube opener, and gloves on the benchtop.

steps.title: Process and Divide Filter
steps.instruction: Prepare the filter for extraction and backup storage.

substeps.instruction: Using clean tweezers, unfold a filter above a clean weigh boat and cut it into two equal halves with clean scissors (alternatively, use sterilized disposable toothpicks and scalpels).
Allow one half to air dry on the weigh boat (since filters were preserved in 95-100% ethanol).
Roll the air-dried filter half and place it into a 2 mL microtube with a Lyse&Spin basket using clean tweezers, toothpicks, or a scalpel.
Store the extraction tube at room temperature if extracting the same day, or at -20 °C if extracting on a subsequent day.
Roll the second filter half and place it into a pre-identified 2 mL Eppendorf Safe-Lock tube; store as backup at -80 °C (alternatively, store in original tubes with 95-100% ethanol at -20 °C).

steps.title: Lysis and Digestion
steps.instruction: Digest the filtrate using T1 solution and Proteinase K under an extractor hood.

substeps.instruction: Change gloves and work under an extractor hood or arm due to Proteinase K.
Prepare a mastermix of 360 µL T1 solution and 50 µL Proteinase K per microtube; work quickly after mixing to avoid self-digestion.
Dispense the mastermix into microtubes, ensuring the filter remains immersed, and mix by inversion for a few seconds.
Incubate in a thermomixer overnight at 56 °C with shaking at 900 rpm (minimum incubation time is 03:00:00).
Centrifuge microtubes at 18,000 g for 00:01:00. If lysis solution remains in the column, repeat centrifugation until all solution has passed through.

steps.title: Eluate Transfer and Buffer Addition
steps.instruction: Transfer the eluate and apply B3 buffer.

substeps.instruction: Transfer the eluate to a new labeled 2 mL microtube to avoid leaking.
Add 400 µL of B3 buffer to each microtube (change pipette tips between tubes or use a multidispense pipette with sterile tips).
Mix by inversion or vortex for a few seconds.
Incubate in the thermomixer for 00:10:00 at 70 °C.

steps.title: Ethanol Precipitation and Column Loading
steps.instruction: Prepare the sample for column binding using ethanol.

substeps.instruction: Add 420 µL of 95-100% ethanol to each microtube (change pipette tips between tubes or use a multidispense pipette with sterile tips).
Mix by inversion or vortex for a few seconds.
Pipet up to 650 µL of the mixture into a MN column placed in a 2 mL collection tube.
Centrifuge at 11,000 g for 00:01:00 and discard the flow-through.
Repeat the loading and centrifugation process until all solution has passed through the column, changing the collection tube as needed.

steps.title: Column Washing
steps.instruction: Wash the DNA bound to the column using BW and B5 buffers.

substeps.instruction: Add 500 µL of BW buffer (change pipette tips or use multidispense pipette), centrifuge at 11,000 g for 00:01:00, and discard the flow-through and collection tube.
Add 600 µL of B5 buffer (change pipette tips or use multidispense pipette), centrifuge at 11,000 g for 00:01:00, and discard the flow-through.
Centrifuge again at 11,000 g for 00:01:00 to dry the column.

steps.title: DNA Elution and Storage
steps.instruction: Elute the DNA and store the resulting extract.

substeps.instruction: Place the column into a labeled 2 mL Eppendorf Safe-Lock microtube.
Add 50 µL of BE buffer (pre-heated to 70 °C) to the center of the membrane.
Incubate at room temperature for 00:01:00.
Repeat the elution process (adding 50 µL BE buffer and incubating) for a second round.
Discard the column and store the eluate at 4 °C (short-term), -20 °C (medium-term), or -80 °C (long-term).
Clean the bench with water, 0.5% sodium hypochlorite solution, and water; OR clean with Alconox, 0.5% sodium hypochlorite solution, and ethanol 70%.
Wipe down pipettes and centrifuges with water, 0.5% sodium hypochlorite solution, water, and ethanol.
Empty liquid bench top trash into the laboratory liquid trash.
Rinse the liquid trash container with water, discard, then clean with water, 0.5% sodium hypochlorite solution, and water.

steps.title: Negative Control Preparation
steps.instruction: Prepare an extraction negative control for each day.

substeps.instruction: Option 1: Humidify a filter (identical material/porosity to project filters) with 250 µL Milli-Q water, add 250 µL 95-100% ethanol, and proceed with the filter division and loading steps.
Option 2: Prepare at the B3 buffer addition step by adding T1 solution only.
